name: Hafgan

attributes.attribute: one of two rival kings of the Otherworld
rival of Arawn, king of Annwn
recovered from any blow after receiving a second blow
defeated by Pwyll in single combat at the end of a year

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Hafgan is the Otherworldly rival whom Arawn of Annwn must face. The name may carry the sense of summer white. Year after year the two were meant to fight one another. Arawn once persuaded Pwyll to wear his shape for a full year. He told Pwyll to deal Hafgan a single blow, for a second would bring him back. Pwyll struck once and laid Hafgan low, then returned to his own world. Some see echoes of Hafgan in the Green Knight who tests Gawain. Others pair him with the Arthurian figure Gromer Somerjoure.

okr.objective: Document Hafgan, the rival king defeated by Pwyll in the Mabinogion.
key_results: Record his name Hafgan or Havgan and its meaning summer song.
Describe his rivalry with Arawn of Annwn and his recovery gift.
Retell Pwyll's year-long substitution and single-combat victory.
